title: Behavioral and neural dynamics for complex motor responses to sound
summary:
This study investigates how people synchronize finger movements with rhythmic sounds and how these processes are related to brain activity. Synchronizing movements to sounds is an important part of everyday human behavior and contributes to functions such as speech, coordination, and auditory-motor interaction. However, it is still unclear which specific movement features people use to align their actions with rhythmic sounds.

In this study, healthy adult participants will perform different finger movements, such as tapping, swiping, and circular movements, while listening to rhythmic auditory stimuli. Finger movements will be recorded using motion tracking and pressure-sensitive devices. In some sessions, brain activity and muscle activity will additionally be recorded using non-invasive measurement methods. The aim of the study is to better understand how movements and sounds are coordinated in the human brain.
conditions: The study investigates healthy adult participants. No disease or clinical population is examined.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Our study will include healthy human participants with normal or corrected-to-normal vision and normal hearing. Since some conditions of our study involves listening to German speech materials (e.g., words and short sentences), participants need to be native speakers of German or have native-level proficiency in German.
Exclusion criteria:
The typical exclusion criteria for psychological studies will apply. In particular, participants will be excluded in case of: 
-	Psychological, psychiatric or neurological diagnoses or treatments, acute or chronic
-	Current use of medication that potentially influences brain activity
-	Acute influence of alcohol or drugs
Additionally, the standard exclusion criteria for MEG and MRI recordings, as outlined here, will be applied:
-	Having a pacemaker, neurostimulator or insulin pumps
-	Having any (surgical) metal implants or prosthesis (this includes retainers – wire behind teeth; braces; metal plates, screws, splinters; fusion pump; aneurism clips; joint replacements; etc)
-	Having any non-removable dentures or braces
-	Having any permanent make-up
-	Having any tattoos
-	Having a metal-containing IUD (intra-uterine device)
-	Being claustrophobic
